Megalomania

meg-uh-loh-MAY-nee-uh · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Megalomania is an obsession with the exercise of power, wealth, or self-importance.

Colleagues began to whisper about the CEO's growing megalomania after he renamed the entire building after himself.

Worked Example

Historians often describe the final years of the emperor's reign as a slow descent into megalomania.

This wasn't ordinary ambition -- it was an all-consuming obsession with his own power and grandeur, which is exactly megalomania.

How Megalomania Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

egomania

egomania: an obsessive focus on oneself

grandiosity

grandiosity: an inflated sense of one's own importance

Antonyms

humility

humility: a modest view of one's own importance

How Strong Is It? — vanity → megalomania → tyranny

vanity vs. megalomania

vanity vs. megalomania: Vanity is an everyday excessive pride in one's appearance or achievements; megalomania is a far more extreme obsession with power itself.

tyranny vs. megalomania

tyranny vs. megalomania: Megalomania describes the inner obsession driving a person; tyranny describes the cruel, oppressive rule that obsession can produce.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of megalomania.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — megalo

root — megalo: great, large (Greek (megas))

root — mania

root — mania: madness, obsession (Greek (mania))

Put it together

Put it together: Megalomania comes from Greek megas ('great') + mania ('madness') -- literally 'greatness madness,' an obsession with one's own grandeur.

Use the root in a new word: megaphone

Use the root in a new word: megaphone: The same megalo- root gives us megaphone (mega- + phone, 'a device for making sound louder') and megabyte.
